chunks: From him, from al-Nahdi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about prostrating on elevated ground, and he said: 'If the place of your forehead is elevated from the place of your body by the height of a brick, there is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum allowable elevation for the forehead during prostration on uneven ground?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *sujood* on uneven surfaces, establishing a practical tolerance for minor topographical variations in prayer spaces. By defining the permissible limit as the height of a brick (approx. 3-4 cm), it balances the spiritual requirement of humility in prostration with the physical realities of daily worship, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease (*rukhas*) in ritual law.
